_about: Each entry puts one known bug back into internal/enforce and the suite must fail. F1 is the #29 fail-open: a session that reports itself locked used to be left alone, and LockedHint is writable by the child. See scripts/mutate.py for what the run checks and what equivalent means. Run: make mutate

mutants.note: the pre-#29 behaviour: one autostart line writing LockedHint would stop enforcement silently forever

mutants.old: return "re-asserted although the session reported itself locked; that report is not evidence the screen is locked"
mutants.note: the forgery attempt leaves no trace in the audit trail, so an operator cannot see that someone was writing the hint

mutants.old: func canNeverConfirm(s platform.Session) bool { return s.Type == "tty" }
mutants.new: func canNeverConfirm(s platform.Session) bool { return false }
mutants.note: a raw VT's permanent ErrUnconfirmed is never escalated; the operator is never told that account is not being locked out

mutants.old: func canNeverConfirm(s platform.Session) bool { return s.Type == "tty" }
mutants.new: func canNeverConfirm(s platform.Session) bool { return true }
mutants.note: every unconfirmed desktop is declared unenforceable, which is a false alarm: the screensaver interface exposes no Locked property, so a locked screen can read unconfirmed forever
the VT verdict is repeated every tick, which is the log flood the once-per-lockout flag exists to prevent

EQUIVALENT, and here is the proof: for the flag to be set, a lock must have been attempted and failed, which requires the override branch not to have run, which leaves overrideActive false — so the very next statement deletes the state entry and the next lockout starts from a fresh one. No input reaches the release with flag set and the entry kept. The line stays as insurance against a future change to that delete condition; TestASecondLockoutReEscalates pins the behaviour it protects, via the delete.

No input reaches the release with the flag set and the entry kept. Anchored on code only, because a pattern spanning a comment breaks whenever the prose is improved.

the pass walks the whole session list on a dead context, so every remaining child is reported unconfirmed during shutdown
